title: Sentinel-1 imagery confirms partial outburst of moraine-dammed lake in upper Trishuli catchment
text: Radar backscatter comparison between 24 and 26 August shows the moraine-dammed lake at roughly 4,650 m in the upper Trishuli catchment has lost an estimated 61 percent of its surface area. ICIMOD assesses this as a confirmed glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF). Peak discharge is propagating down the Trishuli river system towards Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts. Downstream authorities were notified at 03:10 NPT on 26 August.

title: Trek groups on the Gosaikunda route turned back this morning
text: Confirmed with two lodge owners: all trekking parties on the Gosaikunda route have been turned back toward the pass. Gosaikunda itself is above the flood line and reported dry, but the descent trail is unusable. Roughly 40 trekkers waiting it out. No injuries reported from Gosaikunda.

title: Special hydrological bulletin: extreme discharge warning for the entire Trishuli basin
text: The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology issues a red-level warning for the Trishuli basin. Gauge stations along the corridor recorded a discharge spike consistent with a glacial lake outburst flood originating in the upper catchment. All riverside communities in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts must move to higher ground immediately. This bulletin supersedes the routine monsoon advisory issued on 25 August.

title: Syabrubesi bus park completely under water as Trishuli surge arrives
text: The bus park at Syabrubesi was submerged within twenty minutes of the surge arriving, according to residents reached by phone before the line dropped. At least fourteen vehicles were carried downstream. Syabrubesi sits at the confluence and took the flood front directly. Shopkeepers describe water rising above the ground floor of buildings along the main street. Local police moved an estimated 300 people to the school on the ridge above Syabrubesi.

title: District Emergency Operation Centre activated at Dhunche
text: The District Emergency Operation Centre in Dhunche is activated at level 2 as of 04:00 NPT. Dhunche is serving as the district coordination point for Rasuwa. All ward chairpersons are instructed to report headcounts to the Dhunche DEOC by radio. Road access south of Dhunche is not confirmed.

title: Press note: rescue operation underway at Syabrubesi
text: Nepal Police confirm a rescue operation is underway at Syabrubesi in Rasuwa district following the flood surge. The bus park area at Syabrubesi is inundated and vehicles have been swept away. Two persons have been rescued from a rooftop. Search continues for an unconfirmed number of missing. Communication with Syabrubesi is intermittent.

title: Video from Syabrubesi: the whole bus park is gone
text: Sending this before the signal drops again. Syabrubesi bus park is completely under water, buses floating. This is the same location where the surge hit first. People are on the roof of the hotel block. Somebody get a helicopter to Syabrubesi.

title: Bailey bridge at Betrawati swept away as Trishuli surges
text: The Bailey bridge at Betrawati, the main crossing linking Nuwakot with Rasuwa, was swept away in the early hours of Wednesday. Betrawati residents say the deck lifted off its abutments shortly after 04:20 NPT. The loss of the Betrawati crossing severs the only all-weather road link into Rasuwa district. Traffic is being held at Betrawati on the Nuwakot side.

title: Betrawati Bailey bridge washed away, Rasuwa road link cut
text: The Bailey bridge over the Trishuli at Betrawati has been washed away by the flood. Officials in Betrawati say the structure failed at around 4:20 in the morning. With the Betrawati bridge gone there is no vehicle route into Rasuwa. Security personnel have closed the approach road at Betrawati.

title: Betrawati bridge is gone. Confirmed.
text: Just spoke to a shopkeeper at Betrawati. The Bailey bridge at Betrawati is gone, not damaged, gone. Nothing is crossing at Betrawati. If you have family in Rasuwa do not try to drive up.

title: Betrawati bridge collapse cuts the only road link to Rasuwa
text: The collapse of the Bailey bridge at Betrawati has cut the sole motorable link between Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts. Betrawati is now the end of the road for relief convoys. Officials at Betrawati said an alternative crossing would take at least a week to install. The Betrawati bazaar area itself reported flooding of ground-floor shops.

title: Sixty households displaced at Ramche in Rasuwa
text: Around sixty households at Ramche in Rasuwa district have been displaced by the flood and associated bank collapse. Ramche ward office is registering displaced families at the health post. The Ramche section of the district road is impassable. Officials at Ramche requested tarpaulins and drinking water.

title: Trishuli Bazar market area inundated, shops evacuated
text: The market area of Trishuli Bazar in Nuwakot was inundated on Wednesday morning. Shopkeepers at Trishuli Bazar had roughly forty minutes of warning after the alert from upstream and moved stock to upper floors. Water in Trishuli Bazar reached about 1.2 metres in the low-lying lanes near the river.

title: Ramche Danda track buried under debris
text: The foot track up to Ramche Danda is buried under debris from a side gully. Ramche Danda is a small hamlet above the Ankhu confluence, about 15 households. Nobody has been up there since yesterday evening. Note this is Ramche Danda, not Ramche in Rasuwa, people keep mixing them up.

title: Bidur municipality evacuates riverside wards
text: Bidur Municipality has evacuated riverside wards 3, 4 and 9 as the flood crest moves downstream. Around 1,200 residents of Bidur have been moved to the campus building and two school compounds. The Bidur municipal office says the crest is expected to pass Bidur by midday.

title: Water level at Battar Chowk right now
text: Posting from Battar. Water at Battar Chowk has come up to the second step of the bus stand. Everyone on the river side of Battar has moved up to the main road. Battar market is closed. Please do not spread rumours, this is what I can actually see.

title: Relief collection point established at Kalikasthan
text: A relief collection point has been established at Kalikasthan in Rasuwa. Donated material should be delivered to the Kalikasthan ward office between 07:00 and 18:00. Kalikasthan is accessible from the Nuwakot side by the ridge road. Onward distribution north of Kalikasthan is not currently possible.

title: Telecom tower at Syabrubesi down, Syabrubesi now unreachable
text: The telecom tower serving Syabrubesi has gone off air, leaving Syabrubesi and the settlements above it without mobile coverage. Nepal Telecom said the Syabrubesi site lost both grid power and its backup generator to flooding. Restoration teams cannot reach Syabrubesi by road. This is the last confirmed report out of Syabrubesi.

title: Bidur hospital on standby, additional beds prepared
text: The district hospital at Bidur has cleared its outpatient wing to prepare 40 additional beds. Bidur hospital has received nine patients with flood-related injuries so far. Blood supplies at Bidur are adequate. Ambulances staged at Bidur cannot proceed north of Betrawati.

title: National disaster response activated for the Trishuli GLOF event
text: The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority has activated the national response framework for the 26 August glacial lake outburst flood in the Trishuli basin. Three districts are declared affected. Search and rescue assets have been tasked. District authorities are instructed to submit headcount returns every six hours. This is incident record 20260826-01.

title: Nepal glacial flood cuts key highway at Galchhi
text: A glacial lake outburst flood in Nepal has cut the Prithvi Highway at Galchhi, disrupting the main road link between Kathmandu and the country west. A section of carriageway at Galchhi was undermined by the swollen Trishuli river. Galchhi is roughly 60 km west of Kathmandu. Authorities said the Galchhi section would remain closed to all traffic.

title: Prithvi Highway blocked at Galchhi after river undercuts carriageway
text: The Prithvi Highway is blocked at Galchhi in Dhading after the Trishuli undercut around 80 metres of carriageway. Vehicles are being held on both sides of Galchhi. The Division Road Office said restoring the Galchhi section depends on the river level dropping.

title: Highway section washed out at Galchhi, Dhading
text: Incident record: highway section washed out at Galchhi, Dhading district. Approximately 80 metres of the Prithvi Highway carriageway at Galchhi lost to bank erosion. No casualties reported at Galchhi. Traffic diversion is not currently feasible.

title: Explainer: what is a glacial lake outburst flood and why are they getting more common
text: A glacial lake outburst flood happens when a natural dam holding back a glacial lake fails, releasing a large volume of water in a short time. Warming in the high Himalaya has increased both the number and the volume of these lakes over the past three decades. Nepal has several thousand glacial lakes, of which a few dozen are classified as potentially dangerous. This piece explains the mechanism and the monitoring gaps.

title: Gajuri riverside settlements placed on alert
text: Riverside settlements around Gajuri in Dhading have been placed on alert as the flood crest moves downstream. The Gajuri rural municipality has asked residents within 100 metres of the bank to move back. Gajuri is a key stop on the Prithvi Highway and has been used to hold stranded vehicles.

title: Gajuri Bazar shops flooded, water in the main lane
text: Water is in the main lane at Gajuri Bazar. Ground-floor shops at Gajuri Bazar have taken about half a metre. People are moving stock upstairs. The highway itself above Gajuri Bazar is still open for now.

title: Thick silt deposits cover farmland at Benighat
text: Farmland around Benighat in Dhading is buried under silt and coarse sand deposited by the flood. Benighat Rorang rural municipality estimates 90 hectares affected. The Benighat ferry point is unusable. Officials at Benighat say the maize crop is a total loss.

title: Gajuri Bhanjyang track blocked, shops cut off
text: The track up to Gajuri Bhanjyang is blocked by a slip. Gajuri Bhanjyang is the ridge settlement above the highway, not the bazaar down by the river. Shops at Gajuri Bhanjyang are cut off and cannot restock. Please be careful, two different places with almost the same name are being reported as one.

title: Benighat Rorang: silt everywhere, fields buried
text: Drove as far as Benighat. Fields around Benighat are under half a metre of sand and silt. The Benighat ferry crossing is finished. Farmers at Benighat say the maize is gone. This is the last update I can give, going back to Dhadingbesi.

title: Shelter headcount at Dhunche: 412 persons
text: The Dhunche DEOC reports 412 persons in three shelters at Dhunche as of 18:00. Dhunche shelters have food stock for four days. The Dhunche DEOC has not received headcount returns from four wards to the north and west and is escalating this to the district administration.

title: Nilkantha designated as relief staging hub for Dhading
text: Nilkantha, the district headquarters of Dhading, has been designated the relief staging hub for the district. Warehousing at Nilkantha is being prepared for incoming consignments. Nilkantha is on higher ground and was not directly flooded. Convoys will be dispatched from Nilkantha once road conditions allow.

title: School at Belkotgadhi opened as shelter for displaced families
text: A secondary school at Belkotgadhi in Nuwakot has been opened as a shelter for families displaced from riverside wards. Belkotgadhi municipality reports 180 people in the shelter. Belkotgadhi itself was not flooded but is hosting displaced households from downstream Bidur.

title: Damage survey begins in Tadi rural municipality
text: A damage survey has begun in Tadi rural municipality of Nuwakot. Tadi officials say the Tadi Khola tributary backed up when the main river crested, flooding low-lying fields. Preliminary figures from Tadi indicate 34 houses with water damage.

title: Shops reopen partially at Trishuli Bazar as water recedes
text: Some shops at Trishuli Bazar in Nuwakot reopened on Thursday as the water receded. Trishuli Bazar traders are clearing mud from the lower lanes. Electricity at Trishuli Bazar has been partially restored. The Trishuli Bazar vegetable market remains closed.

title: Meghang road clearing underway with one excavator
text: One excavator working the Meghang road. Meghang rural municipality had three slips on the approach. Should be through by tomorrow if it does not rain again. Meghang ward office is coordinating.

title: Ramche Danda still cut off, nobody has walked in yet
text: Following up on Ramche Danda. Still cut off. Nobody from the municipality has walked in to Ramche Danda yet. Fifteen households up there and no contact. Again: Ramche Danda in Dhading, not Ramche in Rasuwa, please do not merge these two in your reporting.

title: First tranche of relief distributed at Ramche
text: The first tranche of relief material reached Ramche in Rasuwa on Thursday afternoon, carried in on foot from Kalikasthan. Ramche ward office distributed tarpaulins and rice to 48 households. Officials at Ramche said a further consignment is needed within three days.

title: Landslide on the Thakre road, watch the top of the slope
text: Clip from the Thakre road showing a slip coming down across the carriageway. Thakre rural municipality. Nobody hurt. Do not stop under this slope, the top of it is still moving.

title: Transit shelter opened at Dhunibesi for stranded travellers
text: A transit shelter has been opened at Dhunibesi in Dhading for travellers stranded by the highway closure. Dhunibesi municipality reports around 260 people using the facility. Dhunibesi was not affected by flooding.

title: Battar market: mud up to the knee in the lower lanes
text: Battar market clean-up day two. Mud up to the knee in the lower lanes at Battar. Two water pumps working. Battar ward office has asked for more shovels and boots, not food, we have food.

title: Fundraiser for families affected by the Trishuli flood — verified organisers
text: We have set up a fundraiser for families affected by the flood. Organisers are verified members of the community and receipts will be posted weekly. Please do not send money to unverified accounts, there are already scam pages circulating. Link in the comments.

title: Water supply intake damaged at Panchakanya
text: The drinking water intake serving Panchakanya rural municipality in Nuwakot was damaged by debris. Panchakanya officials say around 900 households are affected. Tankers are supplying Panchakanya twice daily.

title: Nepal: Trishuli GLOF — Flash Update No. 3
text: Flash Update No. 3 on the glacial lake outburst flood in the Trishuli basin. Three districts remain affected. Access constraints continue to limit verification in the upper corridor, where road and telecommunication links are severed. Reported figures should be treated as incomplete: the absence of reports from some areas reflects access and communication failure rather than absence of impact.

title: Engineering team deployed to Bidur for temporary crossing assessment
text: A Nepal Army engineering team has been deployed to Bidur to assess options for a temporary crossing. The team will work forward from Bidur towards the damaged sections upstream. Equipment is being staged at Bidur.

title: Power restored across most of Belkotgadhi
text: Power is back across most of Belkotgadhi. Belkotgadhi municipality says the two remaining feeders should be live tonight. Shelter at the Belkotgadhi school still running.

title: Thakre detour is open, one lane, slow
text: The Thakre detour is open. One lane, very slow, expect two hours. Thakre rural municipality has traffic marshals at both ends. Do not attempt it at night.

title: National Situation Report No. 4 — Trishuli GLOF
text: National Situation Report No. 4. Reporting coverage remains partial. Fourteen local units in the affected corridor have not submitted a headcount return since 26 August. The Authority notes that these gaps are concentrated in the upper corridor where road and telecommunication access is severed, and cautions against interpreting the absence of returns as an absence of need.

title: First convoy dispatched from the Nilkantha hub
text: The first relief convoy has been dispatched from the staging hub at Nilkantha. Nilkantha warehouse staff loaded tarpaulins, rice and water purification tablets. The convoy will move as far as road conditions permit.

title: Temporary foot crossing being rigged at Betrawati
text: They are rigging a cable foot crossing at Betrawati. Betrawati side is crowded with people waiting to get across. Nothing motorised is crossing at Betrawati and will not for weeks.

title: Advisory: elevated landslide risk along the saturated river corridor
text: Slopes along the affected river corridor remain saturated. The Department advises that secondary landslide risk is elevated for at least the next 72 hours, particularly on slopes undercut by the flood. Any renewed rainfall over 40 mm in 24 hours should be treated as a trigger threshold.

title: Nepal highway partially reopened at Galchhi after flood damage
text: The Prithvi Highway has been partially reopened at Galchhi with a single-lane diversion, officials said. Light vehicles are being allowed through Galchhi during daylight hours. Heavy goods traffic remains held at Galchhi.

title: Gajuri section running single lane, long queues
text: The Gajuri section of the highway is running single lane with long queues in both directions. Traffic police at Gajuri are releasing vehicles in batches. Gajuri bazaar shops have reopened.

title: Three injured as bus overturns near Narayanghat in Chitwan
text: Three passengers were injured when a bus overturned on the East-West Highway near Narayanghat in Chitwan on Saturday morning. Police said the driver lost control on a bend. The injured were taken to Bharatpur Hospital. The vehicle was travelling from Butwal.

title: Dhunche DEOC daily update: shelter and access status
text: Dhunche DEOC daily update. Shelter population at Dhunche now 388. Road access south from Dhunche remains cut at multiple points. The Dhunche DEOC has still received no return from four wards to the north and west and repeats its escalation to the district administration.

title: Third day of clean-up at Trishuli Bazar
text: Clean-up continued for a third day at Trishuli Bazar. Municipal crews and volunteers cleared mud from the main lanes at Trishuli Bazar. Traders at Trishuli Bazar estimate losses in the tens of millions of rupees.

title: Press note: checkpoint status at Betrawati
text: A police checkpoint remains in place at Betrawati. Only authorised relief personnel are permitted beyond Betrawati on foot. Nepal Police remind the public that the Betrawati vehicle crossing is destroyed and no motorised traffic can proceed.

title: Day four briefing at Nilkantha: access remains the constraint
text: At the day four briefing in Nilkantha, district officials said access, not supply, is now the binding constraint. Stocks are adequate at Nilkantha but cannot be moved into the upper corridor. Officials at Nilkantha said helicopter tasking is being requested.

title: Bidur ward 4 update — people are going home
text: Bidur ward 4 update. Water is well down and families are going back into their houses. Bidur municipality is doing a house-by-house safety check. If your house in Bidur has a cracked wall do not sleep in it, report it at the ward office.
